Shared-memory client setup and sign request/response handling for keyguard.

# Purpose
This file implements the client side of a keyguard signing path. The [`fd_keyguard_client_new`](<#fd_keyguard_client_new>) function initializes an `fd_keyguard_client_t` object in shared memory and binds it to request and response message caches and data caches. It stores cache depth, sequence state, workspace pointers, chunk bounds, and the maximum request size. The code uses `fd_mcache_depth`, `fd_wksp_containing`, `fd_dcache_compact_chunk0`, and `fd_dcache_compact_wmark` to set up the shared-memory layout for later message exchange.

The [`fd_keyguard_client_sign`](<#fd_keyguard_client_sign>) function sends sign data to the request cache and waits for a 64-byte signature in the response cache. It checks that the input size does not exceed `request_mtu`, copies the data into the request data cache, publishes a request fragment with `fd_mcache_publish`, and advances the request sequence and chunk pointer. It then waits for a matching response fragment with `FD_MCACHE_WAIT`, validates that the response chunk is inside the expected range, copies the signature into the caller buffer, and checks that the response was not overrun while it was being read.
